title: BEE/RG/TDB trace correlation across a controlled state mutation
question: During two otherwise identical Artisan renders, does a controlled Gaussian Blur value mutation produce observable changes in BEE evaluation/cache/work-queue, MixHashGuid, TDB stream, and RG cache-node trace activity?
source_note: The SDK 25.6 Artie-derived v5 probe starts dvacore trace capture in FrameSetup when available, spans the frame lifecycle through FrameSetdown, and retains Render as a fallback capture path. It labels each capture A/B and restores the previous handler, master volume, stderr handle and category volumes afterward.

environment.ae_version: user-run target: installed AE 26.3; probe compiled against SDK 25.6
environment.notes: Trace wrapper also passed standalone ABI smoke tests against installed AE 25.6 and 26.3 dvacore.dll. Full provider behavior is evaluated only in the user-run host.

hypotheses.prediction: Target BEE/RG/TDB/GUID categories emit trace lines inside the real host render window.
hypotheses.falsified_by: No target-category lines occur between AEIG_TRACE_BEGIN/END despite successful rendering.

hypotheses.prediction: Changing the blur state between pass A and B changes at least part of the identity/evaluation/cache/RG trace footprint.
hypotheses.falsified_by: A and B produce indistinguishable target-category trace footprints under a confirmed state change.

procedure: User installs the canonical AEIG L5 Artie probe while AE is closed and launches a disposable blank session.
The script renders pass A with blur 10, mutates only blur to 75, then renders pass B.
The Artisan labels each frame using current-pass.txt; FrameSetup->FrameSetdown is the primary trace window and Render is a fallback when no frame-level window is active.
The probe restores the original master trace handler, master/category volumes and stderr handle after every capture.
analyze_rg_trace_experiment.py partitions the raw trace by pass and reports target-category activity without assuming that category-name frequency alone identifies a unique internal object.
